decisive_items: bilateral naevus flammeus along the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve
iris heterochromia with diffuse hyperpigmentation and evenly distributed micronodular elevations on the iris surface
choroidal thickness of 2.2 mm in the right eye versus 1.4 mm in the left
response.rationale: The facial angioma in trigeminal distribution plus ipsilateral ocular findings (iris heterochromia, choroidal thickening, elevated IOP) are classic for Sturge-Weber syndrome. Ocular melanosis is a partial mimic but lacks the facial nevus flammeus and choroidal thickening. Glaucoma is a secondary complication, not the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Diffuse hyperpigmentation alone is insufficient; lacks facial angioma and choroidal thickening.
Elevated IOP and trabecular hyperpigmentation are secondary to the underlying syndrome, not the primary diagnosis.
